changes: Explicit recovery bypasses uncertain/activity/pending-work admission and preempts worker configuration, but cannot enter a concurrent root configuration transaction or receipt rotation.
Recovery generation increments on emergency admission and is checked at every old non-root beforeWrite boundary, including after maintenance clears.
ManagerClient reserves one bounded independent emergency helper slot; ordinary queued helpers do not start while it lives. Ordinary in-flight helper and real root management lock are retained.
Every helper slot remains occupied until actual close, including reply-before-exit, rejection and timeout. No retries, no deleting flock and no root configuration preemption.

Manager recover reuses existing restart: stop both cgroups with existing 25-second SIGTERM/SIGKILL policy; confirm empty; owner-bound journal recovery preserves unknown receipts; start and health check.
The root helper remains in its existing independently owned systemd management unit, outside the gateway/worker cgroups being stopped.

Independent review found the original shared maintenance boolean also blocked recovery during worker configuration. The final implementation uses unique root/worker/receipt maintenance owners: recovery may replace only a worker owner; obsolete finally blocks cannot release the new owner. Root configuration and receipt rotation remain non-preemptible.

First Linux report complete=false after successful tests because removing own unit files left not-found/failed tombstones. Both had PID0 and empty cgroup. Separate exact fixture reset-failed cleanup passed; original result untouched.

limits: No production instance restart, configuration change, deployment, model inference or external MCP call performed.

Systemd probe substitutes isolated sleeping programs for application/native/MCP bodies and isolates ownership/release checks/unit refresh/application health. Actual process stop, cgroup emptiness, privilege drop and SQLite recovery are exercised.
A real pending root configuration transaction still owns management.lock; recovery reports bounded busy/recovery-required rather than deleting locks or cancelling uncertain writes.

A dead gateway/blocked HTTP event loop requires independent server-console/SSH operations. Kernel uninterruptible tasks, unavailable systemd or failed empty-cgroup proof cannot be truthfully declared stopped.
Unknown external side effects are not reversed; stopped task/OAuth receipts stay unknown and are never automatically replayed.
Windows subprocess proves transport scheduling, not Linux flock; real Linux cgroup stop is separately evidenced.
